extracted.intended_audience: donors and potential grantees interested in effective global health and development funding
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria used by the Global Health and Development Fund (an Effective Altruism Fund managed by GiveWell leadership) for recommending and making grants intended to improve health or economic empowerment in low- and middle-income countries. Covers target populations, types of interventions, risk profile, and evidence/underfunding considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund primary aim
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to improve the health or economic empowerment of people around the world as effectively as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Fund's overarching objective and shapes what kinds of grants it will recommend and prioritize. Emphasis on effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus: direct provision of healthcare or preventive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Support projects that directly provide healthcare, or preventive measures that will improve health, well-being, or life expectancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the site include distributing bednets to prevent malaria and supporting seasonal malaria chemoprevention programs. Priority is given to interventions with clear, direct effects on health outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus: direct services to raise incomes or improve economic conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Support projects that directly provide services that raise incomes or otherwise improve economic conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes programs that increase economic empowerment in low- and middle-income settings; may fund interventions like agricultural programs, livelihoods support, or other direct income-raising services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus: assistance to governments on policy design and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide assistance to governments in the design and implementation of effective policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund may fund technical assistance, policy design, or implementation support when these are expected to lead to large-scale benefits for poor populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad remit for other activities serving poorest regions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund has a broad remit and may fund other activities whose ultimate purpose is to serve people living in the poorest regions of the world, for example by raising additional funds or by exploring novel financing arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: supporting organizations that raise additional funds (One for the World) or novel financing arrangements (Instiglio). The Fund is not limited strictly to direct service delivery if the ultimate purpose serves the poorest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline and comparative expectation of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund manager recommends grants to GiveWell top charities as a baseline, but will recommend higher-risk grants they believe to be more effective (in expectation) than GiveWell top charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantmaking balances a baseline of well-vetted, evidence-backed charities with opportunistic, higher-risk bets when expected value exceeds that baseline. The Fund explicitly uses GiveWell top charities as a benchmark for 'straightforward' giving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of risk profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: The fund makes grants with a variety of different risk profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitability of particular grants depends on their expected effectiveness and risk; the Fund will include both lower-risk, well-established interventions and higher-risk, potentially higher-impact opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population: poorest regions / low- and middle-income countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund makes grants to organizations directly serving people in low- and middle-income countries, typically in the poorest regions of the world where the need for healthcare and economic empowerment is greatest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes geographic and population targeting toward places with greatest need (e.g., where many people live under the international poverty line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-backed, thoroughly vetted, underfunded (GiveWell baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: GiveWell recommends charities that are evidence-backed, thoroughly vetted, and underfunded; the Fund uses GiveWell expertise as part of its baseline recommendation set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using GiveWell-recommended charities as baseline grants, the Fund is implicitly applying criteria of evidence quality, thorough vetting, and underfunding as reasons to prioritize those charities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on tractability and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Global health and development is a highly tractable area: even small donations can have a huge impact. The problem is also very large in scale, and there is often room for more funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund favors opportunities where interventions are tractable (small donations produce large effects), where the scale of the problem is large, and where additional funding can materially change outcomes (room for more funding). The page cites global poverty and child mortality statistics to motivate these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant types and activities supported
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund supports a range of activities including direct program delivery, planning and evaluation work (e.g., planning RCTs), research and advocacy, and pilot or higher-risk projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featured grants include support for planning RCTs, research and advocacy to reduce lead exposure, program planning and data gathering for agricultural programs, and support for seasonally targeted health interventions—indicating willingness to fund both operational programs and evidence-building activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial expertise and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund is managed by GiveWell co-founder Elie Hassenfeld and GiveWell staff who have extensive experience analyzing unusually promising opportunities in the global health and development space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manager's experience and GiveWell's research capacity are presented as part of the rationale for grant selection credibility; this criterion suggests grants are evaluated by staff with demonstrated expertise in identifying high-impact opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor suitability / alignment with risk preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund is suitable for donors who want to take calculated risks, but who support more straightforward giving when the fund manager is unable to identify riskier opportunities they believe to be more effective (in expectation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donors with strong preferences for a particular risk profile or type of benefit may prefer other options (e.g., directly supporting GiveWell top charities if they prefer lower-risk giving). This helps match donor risk tolerance to fund strategy.
